text:
maria (PM): Heads-up — I'm seeing inconsistent behavior for route presets across hosted vs Dedicated when users hit the 'Save for route' flow. Some customers think presets are per-route, others expect cross-tier defaults. Need quick sync on expected UX + API semantics.

alex (eng): Noted. Do we have a hard product decision or is this still exploratory?

maria (PM): Still exploratory. We need to pick an approach before the console rollout next week. Options: 1) enforce per-route only, 2) allow cross-tier inheritance with explicit override, 3) allow account-level defaults that per-route can opt out of.

nina (design): For the console, my preference is explicit inheritance with a clear affordance: a small badge "inherited" and an "Edit default" CTA. Avoid magic.

ken (platform): From the backend side, 2 is doable but we need to standardize the API shape. Right now we have two endpoints: `GET /presets?route_id=...` and `GET /defaults?scope=account`. They return slightly different schemas which is the root cause.

alex (eng): Can we converge to a single union shape? e.g., `schema.presets[].applies_to: ["route","account","model"]` and a `inherited_from` field when applicable. That would simplify client logic and telemetry.

sam (sre): Telemetry/quotas question: if we let account defaults cascade into routes, we need to be careful about previewing token burn estimates. Customers expect per-route cost preview; inheritance might hide surprises.

maria (PM): Good point — we need inline cost hints in the save modal. If a route inherits a preset with heavier model, show a delta.

nina (design): UX mock: small inline line under preset name: "+2.1k tokens per 1k requests (inherited from Org Default)". Click opens an expanded diff.

ken (platform): Implementation notes: we'll add `inherited_from: "org_default|team_default|route_default"` string. That keeps schema flat. Also add `preview_cost_tokens` numeric field.

alex (eng): That sounds fine. One concern: we currently use different sampling rates for telemetry on account-level vs per-route events. Need to unify so regression alerts don't miss inherited changes.

sam (sre): I recommend tagging events with `preset_scope` and `effective_scope` so telemetry can filter both the origin and the effective application. Then sampling can be kept consistent.

maria (PM): Agree — telemetry contract: include `preset_scope`, `origin_preset_id`, `effective_preset_id`, `changed_by`, and `preview_cost_delta` for saves/rollouts.

alex (eng): Rollout plan idea: start with read-only inheritance in console (show inherited presets but disable applying them as defaults). Rollout A/B: 10% of orgs get editability. Monitor errors and cost regressions.

nina (design): If read-only first, we should still surface the edit path to explain how to change defaults (link to org settings) — reduces confusion.

ken (platform): API change timeline: I can land a compatibility shim that returns both old and new fields for 2 weeks. After that we flip clients. PR: internal/rfcs#245.

alex (eng): I'll add client-side mapping and a small migration test. Also add feature flag `cross_tier_presets_edit` to gate writes.

sam (sre): Add an alert when `preview_cost_delta` exceeds threshold (e.g., 20% token increase) during rollouts — we should block auto-updates in that case.

maria (PM): Action items: (1) ken to share API draft + compatibility plan by EOD, (2) nina to produce two quick mocks (read-only + editable) by tomorrow noon, (3) alex to add feature flag and unit tests, (4) sam to propose telemetry/alert thresholds. I'll coordinate a 20-minute sync after mocks.

ken (platform): Posted API draft: https://internal.redwood/PRs/245 — fields shown, backward-compat notes in the top comment.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered for `platform/compat-shim` to staging at 2025-09-14T15:12:03Z :rocket:

alex (eng): Saw the PR, will review now. If we can keep the response flat as discussed it's low risk.

nina (design): Quick question: for inherited presets, do we allow per-model overrides within a route? e.g., route uses model A by default but some sub-endpoints want a cheaper model.

maria (PM): Prefer to allow per-model override but hide complexity in the initial rollout. Keep the first pass simpler: route-level presets only then expand to per-model overrides in next sprint.

sam (sre): Agreed. One more ops note: document expected fallback behavior when Dedicated capacity lacks a model. Should auto-fallback to compatible quantized variant and surface that in the preset UI as "fallback model".

ken (platform): We'll include `fallback_model_id` in the preset response and an `is_fallback` boolean on active allocations.

maria (PM): Perfect. Thanks team — I'll schedule the sync after nina posts mocks. :thumbsup:
